nodes.rationale: Middleware-based validation against SubscriptionPlan.features chosen for reusability across routes and centralized logic; rejected alternatives were controller-level checking (too repetitive) and frontend-only gating (not secure).

nodes.label: Multi-Mode Simultaneous Tenant Modules Decision
nodes.rationale: Tenant.modules JSON allows gym+POS+restaurant to run simultaneously rather than exclusively, enabling hybrid business models and more revenue streams.

nodes.label: Per-Station Printer Configuration Decision
nodes.rationale: PrinterDevice model configured per-station with tenant admin control, since one tenant may have multiple locations/POS stations and admins should self-manage printer setup without superadmin intervention.

nodes.label: Maintain Existing Transaction Architecture Decision
nodes.rationale: Keep the existing Transaction model and expand the polymorphic TransactionItem rather than rewriting, since the system is already proven and this preserves backward compatibility with MembershipPayment.

nodes.label: Database-Backed Sequence Management Decision
nodes.rationale: SequenceCounter model chosen over in-memory counters for reliability across restarts, better race-condition prevention via pessimistic locking, and easier auditing/monitoring.

nodes.label: Third-Party Credential Encryption Decision
nodes.rationale: At-rest encryption with tenant-specific keys chosen for security compliance, isolating credentials between tenants and mitigating leakage risk on database breach.

nodes.label: Model Loading Architecture Pattern
nodes.rationale: Controllers must import Sequelize model instances from the main src/models/index.js db object (where models are initialized and associated), not directly from module definition folders like src/modules/restaurant/models, which only export uninitialized model-definition functions.

nodes.label: Explicit Undefined Check Pattern for Field Preservation
nodes.rationale: Use `field !== undefined ? field : existing.field` instead of `field || existing.field` when preserving optional update fields, since OR-based fallback misbehaves with falsy-but-valid values; validation that rejects a status change should also only trigger when the incoming value differs from the existing value, not merely when it is present.

nodes.rationale: The prior flat boolean `features` object didn't scale as the feature count grew, so features were regrouped into 8 semantic categories (modules, limits, transactions, payments, printing, restaurant, integrations, support) to organize the PlanFormModal UI, enable per-category counters and collapsible sections, and mirror the backend's Feature Registry; old flat fields (maxUsers, maxMembers at root) are preserved for backward compatibility.

nodes.label: Payment Flow Option A (Payment First)
nodes.rationale: Option A (pending-then-activate) was chosen so subscriptions can be manually assigned and invoiced by a super admin before an automated payment gateway exists: a subscription is created 'pending', an invoice auto-generates (due in 7 days), and the subscription only auto-activates once a payment covering the invoice total is manually recorded. This defers Flow 2 (public registration with payment gateway) to a later phase once automated payment processing is required.

nodes.label: Session-based (vs Order-based) Billing Report
nodes.rationale: Session-based reporting was chosen over order-based because a single order can bundle multiple tests (e.g. a package of CFIT+PAPI+EPPS), so counting at order level undercounts actual test usage; sessions also carry per-test verified/unverified status, a completion timestamp (`completedAt`, more accurate than `createdAt`), and duration — all needed for accurate per-test invoicing, quality control, and client dispute resolution.
